chain_papers: MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP
Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection

analysis.MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detect: Builds on MVFA's adapters but separates normal and abnormal evidence into dual adapter branches and trains them with a SigLIP (pairwise sigmoid) loss that tolerates many-to-one image/prompt relations. Relevant: a sigmoid per-patch loss can down-weight uncertain targets, which is what noisy pseudo-masks need.
analysis.Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype: Builds on MadCLIP-style fixed references by re-centring normal and abnormal prototypes per image with a bounded gate, and keeps a non-parametric normal memory. Relevant: per-image re-centring of the normal reference reduces false positives caused by anatomy that differs between images of the same dataset.

seeds.rationale: Pseudo-masks defined against a dataset-wide normal bank (the problem's rule) mark anatomically unusual but healthy patches as anomalous. ReCAP shows that a per-image, bounded re-centring of the normal reference fixes static-anchor errors, and MadCLIP shows that a sigmoid loss handles many-to-one supervision. Combining them gives pseudo-masks with a per-image normal reference and an explicit ignore band for uncertain patches, so the segmentation adapters are only trained where the pseudo-label is confident.
seeds.title: Bounded prototype pseudo-masks with an ignore band for mask-free MVFA segmentation
seeds.summary: Derive pseudo-masks from distances to per-image re-centred normal prototypes, train the segmentation adapters only on confident patches with a sigmoid loss, and measure how much mask-supervised localisation is recovered.
seeds.research_idea: Independent variable: supervision of seg_adapters (true masks vs. pseudo-masks, with or without per-image re-centring and ignore band) and the number of masked source datasets whose masks are removed (0, 1, 3). For each source dataset, 32 normal prototypes per level are obtained by k-means on frozen CLIP level-4 patch features of its normal training images. For an abnormal training image, each prototype is re-centred toward the image's own mean patch feature by a bounded step (gate g = 0.2, step norm clipped to 0.5 x the prototype's within-cluster radius). A patch's distance d is its minimum distance to the re-centred prototypes; patches with d above the 99th percentile of normal-to-normal distances (source validation) are labelled anomalous, below the 95th percentile normal, and those in between are ignored. Dependent variables: pixel AUROC and Dice on held-out masked modalities, pseudo-mask IoU against true masks, and image AUROC.
seeds.hypothesis: Training MVFA's segmentation adapters on bounded-prototype pseudo-masks with an ignore band recovers at least 85% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC gain over frozen CLIP on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC, and at least 5 points more pseudo-mask IoU than the static-bank rule of the problem statement.
seeds.method: 1) New script make_pseudo_masks.py: for each source dataset, extract frozen CLIP ViT-L/14-336 layer-24 patch features (17x17 grid at 240 px) of normal train images; run k-means (k=32, 5 restarts) to get prototypes P_k and radii r_k (mean distance of members). 2) For each abnormal train image: m = mean patch feature; P_k' = P_k + clip(0.2 (m - P_k), max_norm = 0.5 r_k). Patch distance d_p = min_k ||f_p - P_k'||_2. 3) Thresholds t_lo, t_hi = 95th/99th percentiles of d over normal source-validation images (computed the same way). Label y_p = 1 if d_p > t_hi, 0 if d_p < t_lo, ignore otherwise; upsample to 240x240 with nearest neighbour; save as .npy masks plus an ignore mask. Normal images get all-zero masks. 4) dataset/medical_zero.py: load pseudo-masks and ignore masks for datasets flagged pseudo; seg_idx >= 0 for all six datasets. 5) train_zero.py: replace Focal + Dice on seg_adapters by a masked sigmoid (SigLIP-style) loss L = mean over non-ignored pixels of softplus(-(2y-1)(t s_p + b)), t, b learnable (init 10, -10), plus Dice on non-ignored pixels; det branch unchanged. 6) Model selection by source-validation pixel AUROC computed against pseudo-masks (no target labels). 7) Hyper-parameters: lr 1e-3 (as in the paper), 50 epochs, batch 16 via gradient accumulation, k=32, g=0.2, percentiles 95/99.
seeds.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on the masked targets BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Checkpoints and all thresholds selected on source-modality validation splits only; MVFA re-run under the same rule as the mask-supervised reference; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: (a) true masks on 3 sources (reference), (b) pseudo-masks replace masks on 1 source, (c) on all 3 sources, (d) (c) plus the image-only datasets as pseudo-mask sources. Ablations: static bank rule (problem statement) vs re-centred prototypes; with vs without ignore band. Metrics: pixel AUROC, Dice at the source-validation-selected threshold, image AUROC, pseudo-mask IoU vs true masks on the three masked datasets. Falsified if condition (c) recovers less than 70% of the gain of (a) over frozen CLIP, or if re-centring does not improve pseudo-mask IoU.
provenance: MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP
Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection

chain_papers: Fine-Tuning CLIP Models with Convolutional Features for Medical Anomaly Detection

analysis.Fine-Tuning CLIP Models with Convolution: Keeps MVFA's multi-level residual adapters but adds a ConvTokenizer so CLIP's image tokens are aligned with raw input details, improving segmentation. Relevant: it identifies the loss of fine detail at the 14-pixel patch grid as a limit of MVFA's localisation, which also limits patch-level pseudo-masks.

seeds.rationale: Patch-level pseudo-masks are 17x17 at 240 px, so each label covers a 14-pixel block and boundaries are wrong almost everywhere along a lesion; Dice supervision on such blocks teaches the adapters blocky maps. MLCA shows that raw-input detail matters for MVFA-style localisation. A cheap way to inject raw detail into the targets is to snap the patch pseudo-mask to image superpixels, so every pseudo-mask boundary follows an intensity edge.
seeds.title: Superpixel-snapped pseudo-masks for mask-free training of MVFA's segmentation adapters
seeds.summary: Refine label-restricted patch pseudo-masks by majority voting inside SLIC superpixels of the raw image before using them as Dice and Focal targets.
seeds.research_idea: Independent variable: target type for seg_adapters: true masks; raw patch pseudo-masks (problem rule); superpixel-snapped pseudo-masks with n_segments in {100, 200, 400}. Snapping: a superpixel is labelled anomalous if the area-weighted mean of the upsampled patch anomaly indicator inside it exceeds 0.5 and the image is labelled abnormal; normal images stay empty. Dependent variables: pseudo-mask Dice/IoU vs. true masks, pixel AUROC and Dice of the trained model on held-out masked modalities, and boundary F1 (2-pixel tolerance).
seeds.hypothesis: Superpixel-snapped pseudo-masks raise pseudo-mask Dice against true masks by at least 8 points over raw patch pseudo-masks on BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC, and MVFA trained on them reaches at least 90% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities, versus at most 80% for raw patch pseudo-masks.
seeds.method: 1) make_pseudo_masks.py: compute the problem's label-restricted patch rule (level-4 features, 99th percentile of normal-to-normal NN distances on source validation) giving a 17x17 binary map per abnormal image. 2) Upsample bilinearly to 240x240 to obtain an indicator a(x). 3) Run skimage.segmentation.slic(image, n_segments=200, compactness=10, channel_axis=None for grey images) on the 240x240 input. 4) For superpixel S: label = 1 if mean_{x in S} a(x) > 0.5. 5) Remove components smaller than 20 pixels. 6) dataset/medical_zero.py reads these masks for all datasets marked pseudo; train_zero.py keeps Focal + Dice unchanged. 7) n_segments selected on source validation by pseudo-mask Dice where masks exist in the source fold (never the target). Hyper-parameters otherwise as MVFA (lr 1e-3, 50 epochs).
seeds.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on the masked targets BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Checkpoints and all thresholds selected on source-modality validation splits only; MVFA re-run under the same rule as the mask-supervised reference; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; raw patch pseudo-masks; snapped pseudo-masks (n_segments 100/200/400); masks removed from 1 and from all 3 masked sources. Metrics: pseudo-mask Dice/IoU/boundary F1; trained-model pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC. Falsified if snapping does not raise pseudo-mask Dice by 8 points or the trained model's pixel AUROC is not higher than with raw patch pseudo-masks.
provenance: Fine-Tuning CLIP Models with Convolutional Features for Medical Anomaly Detection

chain_papers: Fed-LoRA: Cross-Domain Generative Knowledge Feedback for Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection

analysis.Fed-LoRA: Cross-Domain Generative Knowle: Synthesises abnormal exemplars tailored to each institution's imaging style with LoRA-adapted generators, showing that synthetic abnormal images with known extents can supplement scarce real ones. Relevant: synthetic lesions come with exact masks, the opposite error profile of pseudo-masks on real lesions.

seeds.rationale: Pseudo-masks on real abnormal images have realistic appearance but noisy extents; synthetic lesions pasted into normal images of the same dataset have exact extents but unrealistic appearance. Fed-LoRA shows synthetic abnormal images help few-shot anomaly detection when tailored to the domain. Training the segmentation adapters on a mixture of the two sources should combine their strengths, and the mixing ratio is the key variable.
seeds.title: Mixing label-restricted pseudo-masks with exact synthetic-lesion masks for mask-free MVFA localisation
seeds.summary: Train MVFA's segmentation adapters on real abnormal images with pseudo-masks plus normal images carrying synthetic lesions with exact masks, and find the mixing ratio that best recovers mask-supervised localisation.
seeds.research_idea: Independent variable: fraction rho of segmentation-branch training samples that are synthetic (0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0), with the rest being real abnormal images with label-restricted pseudo-masks (problem rule). Synthetic lesions are created per source dataset from its own images: a random elliptical region (area 0.5-8% of the image) of a normal image is replaced by a Poisson-blended patch cut from an abnormal image's pseudo-anomalous area (so texture is realistic), or by an intensity-perturbed blob (Gaussian intensity shift of +-0.3 x local std) when no anomalous patch exists; the mask is the pasted region. Dependent variables: pixel AUROC and Dice on held-out masked modalities, image AUROC, and the false-positive rate on normal test images at the source-selected threshold.
seeds.hypothesis: A mixture with rho between 0.25 and 0.5 recovers at least 90% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities and beats both pure pseudo-masks (rho = 0) and pure synthesis (rho = 1) by at least 2 pixel-AUROC points.
seeds.method: 1) make_pseudo_masks.py: compute label-restricted pseudo-masks for real abnormal source images (problem rule). 2) synth.py: function synth_lesion(normal_img, donor_img, donor_mask) using cv2.seamlessClone (Poisson) with an elliptical mask; fallback blob perturbation. 3) dataset/medical_zero.py: a MixedSegDataset that, per iteration, draws a synthetic sample with probability rho, else a real abnormal sample with pseudo-mask (normal images also drawn as in MVFA). 4) train_zero.py: unchanged losses (Focal + Dice on seg branch, BCE on det branch); synthetic images labelled abnormal for the det branch. 5) Select rho and checkpoint on source-validation pixel AUROC against pseudo-masks (no target data). Hyper-parameters as MVFA (lr 1e-3, 50 epochs, 240 px).
seeds.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on the masked targets BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Checkpoints and all thresholds selected on source-modality validation splits only; MVFA re-run under the same rule as the mask-supervised reference; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: rho in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1}; reference with true masks. Ablation: Poisson-blended real texture vs intensity blobs only. Metrics: pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC, normal-image FPR. Falsified if no intermediate rho beats both extremes by 2 points or if the best mixture recovers less than 80% of the mask-supervised gain.
provenance: Fed-LoRA: Cross-Domain Generative Knowledge Feedback for Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection

chain_papers: Bridging Vision Foundation Model Priors with CLIP for Spatial-aware Few-shot Anomaly Detection in Medical Images

analysis.Bridging Vision Foundation Model Priors: Injects a structural affinity prior from DINO into CLIP features through a VFM-enhanced adapter, because DINO patch features are spatially coherent and follow lesion boundaries, and stores compact normal/abnormal prototypes for few-shot use. Relevant: DINO affinity can spread a sparse anomalous seed over the coherent lesion region.

seeds.rationale: Label-restricted pseudo-masks from CLIP features are fragmented: only the most atypical patches pass the 99th-percentile threshold, so lesions appear as scattered seeds. Spatial-FAD shows that DINO's patch affinities capture anatomical structure and lesion boundaries better than CLIP. Propagating the confident seeds over a DINOv2 affinity graph turns fragments into coherent regions while staying inside the abnormal image, which should give the segmentation adapters better targets.
seeds.title: DINOv2-affinity propagation of label-restricted pseudo-masks for mask-free MVFA training
seeds.summary: Grow confident CLIP pseudo-mask seeds over a DINOv2 patch-affinity graph with a random walk, and train MVFA's segmentation adapters on the propagated masks.
seeds.research_idea: Independent variable: target type: true masks; seed-only pseudo-masks (problem rule); DINOv2-affinity propagated pseudo-masks with walk length T in {1, 3, 5}. Affinity A_ij = exp(cos(g_i, g_j)/tau) over the 8-neighbourhood and top-10 feature neighbours of DINOv2 ViT-B/14 patch features g at 224 px (16x16 grid), row-normalised; propagated score s_T = A^T s_0 with s_0 the binary seed map; final mask = s_T > 0.5 x max(s_T) intersected with the image being labelled abnormal. Dependent variables: pseudo-mask Dice vs true masks; pixel AUROC and Dice of the trained model on held-out masked modalities.
seeds.hypothesis: DINOv2-affinity propagation with T = 3 increases pseudo-mask Dice by at least 10 points over seed-only pseudo-masks, and MVFA trained on the propagated masks attains at least 90% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities.
seeds.method: 1) make_pseudo_masks.py: compute seed maps with the problem rule (CLIP level-4, 99th percentile on source validation). 2) Load DINOv2 ViT-B/14 via torch.hub ('facebookresearch/dinov2', 'dinov2_vitb14'); extract normalised patch tokens at 224 px. 3) Resample seeds to the 16x16 DINO grid; build sparse A (8-neighbours + 10 feature NNs, tau = 0.1). 4) s_T = A^T s_0, T = 3 (selected on source validation where masks exist in the source fold); threshold at 0.5 max; upsample to 240 px. 5) dataset/medical_zero.py loads the propagated masks; train_zero.py unchanged (Focal + Dice). 6) Runtime: one forward pass of DINOv2 per abnormal image, minutes on one GPU. Hyper-parameters as MVFA.
seeds.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on the masked targets BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Checkpoints and all thresholds selected on source-modality validation splits only; MVFA re-run under the same rule as the mask-supervised reference; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; seed-only; propagated with T in {1,3,5}; masks removed from 1 and 3 sources. Ablation: CLIP-feature affinity instead of DINOv2 affinity (isolates the structural prior). Metrics: pseudo-mask Dice/IoU, trained pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC. Falsified if DINOv2 propagation does not beat CLIP-affinity propagation and seed-only masks on pseudo-mask Dice.
provenance: Bridging Vision Foundation Model Priors with CLIP for Spatial-aware Few-shot Anomaly Detection in Medical Images

chain_papers: AA-CLIP: Enhancing Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection via Anomaly-Aware CLIP
PSMP-CLIP: Patch-Prompt SAM and Multi-Semantic Prompting for CLIP-Based Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection

analysis.AA-CLIP: Enhancing Zero-Shot Anomaly Det: Adapts CLIP with residual adapters in two stages: it first creates anomaly-aware text anchors that separate normal and abnormal semantics, then aligns patch features with them. Relevant: well-separated anchors give a cleaner patch anomaly signal from which prompts or seeds can be sampled.
analysis.PSMP-CLIP: Patch-Prompt SAM and Multi-Se: Builds on CLIP patch anomaly maps by sampling point prompts directly from intermediate patch features and passing them to SAM2, which returns precise masks and avoids threshold drift. Relevant: SAM2 can turn coarse patch evidence into object-shaped masks without training.

seeds.rationale: Label-restricted pseudo-masks give reliable locations but poor shapes. PSMP-CLIP shows that point prompts sampled from patch anomaly evidence let SAM2 produce precise masks, and AA-CLIP shows that separated anchors make the patch evidence cleaner. Using SAM2 as a mask former on top of the problem's pseudo-mask seeds should produce lesion-shaped targets for MVFA's segmentation adapters without any human masks.
seeds.title: SAM2-formed pseudo-masks from label-restricted patch prompts for mask-free MVFA localisation
seeds.summary: Prompt SAM2 with the most anomalous label-restricted patches of each abnormal source image and train MVFA's segmentation adapters on the returned masks.
seeds.research_idea: Independent variable: target type: true masks; patch pseudo-masks (problem rule); SAM2-formed pseudo-masks with n_points in {1, 3, 5} positive prompts (patch centres with the largest NN distance above threshold, at least 2 patches apart) and 3 negative prompts from the lowest-distance patches. Masks whose area exceeds 40% of the image or whose overlap with the patch pseudo-mask is below 0.2 are rejected (fallback to the patch pseudo-mask). Dependent variables: pseudo-mask Dice vs true masks; trained model's pixel AUROC and Dice on held-out masked modalities.
seeds.hypothesis: SAM2-formed pseudo-masks with 3 positive prompts raise pseudo-mask Dice by at least 12 points over patch pseudo-masks on BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC, and MVFA trained on them recovers at least 90% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities.
seeds.method: 1) make_pseudo_masks.py: compute patch NN distances and the label-restricted rule. 2) sam_refine.py: load SAM2 (hiera-base-plus checkpoint from the official repository); for each abnormal source image, select up to n_points positive patch centres (scaled to image coordinates) and 3 negative ones; call SAM2ImagePredictor.predict(point_coords, point_labels, multimask_output=True) and keep the mask with the highest predicted IoU. 3) Apply the rejection rules; save masks. 4) dataset/medical_zero.py loads them; train_zero.py unchanged (Focal + Dice). 5) n_points selected on source validation (where source masks exist). Runtime: one SAM2 call per abnormal image. Hyper-parameters as MVFA.
seeds.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on the masked targets BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Checkpoints and all thresholds selected on source-modality validation splits only; MVFA re-run under the same rule as the mask-supervised reference; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; patch pseudo-masks; SAM2-formed with 1/3/5 points; masks removed from 1 and 3 sources. Ablation: without rejection rules; MedSAM-style medical SAM weights if available as an alternative mask former. Metrics: pseudo-mask Dice/IoU and rejection rate; trained pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC. Falsified if SAM2 masks do not improve pseudo-mask Dice by at least 5 points on at least two of the three masked datasets.
provenance: AA-CLIP: Enhancing Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection via Anomaly-Aware CLIP
PSMP-CLIP: Patch-Prompt SAM and Multi-Semantic Prompting for CLIP-Based Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection

chain_papers: G-Anomaly: A Pyramid Graph Transformer-Based Vision-Language Model for General Industrial Anomaly Detection

analysis.G-Anomaly: A Pyramid Graph Transformer-B: Industrial anomaly detection with a pyramid graph transformer that preserves structural relations between image regions and a multi-level domain adapter. It does not build on the medical setting but its insight, that regional topology distinguishes anomalies from texture, applies to pseudo-mask cleaning.

seeds.rationale: Label-restricted pseudo-masks contain isolated false positives (healthy but rare anatomy) and holes inside lesions. G-Anomaly shows that modelling the topology of image regions separates anomalies from normal texture. A pairwise graph model over patches (a dense CRF on the patch grid with feature and spatial affinities) can enforce that anomalous patches form coherent regions, removing isolated false positives and filling holes before the masks supervise MVFA.
seeds.title: Graph-regularised pseudo-masks: CRF smoothing on the patch grid for mask-free MVFA training
seeds.summary: Clean label-restricted pseudo-masks with a fully connected CRF over patches whose unary term is the NN-distance score and whose pairwise term uses CLIP feature similarity and position.
seeds.research_idea: Independent variable: target type: true masks; raw label-restricted pseudo-masks; CRF-regularised pseudo-masks with pairwise weight w in {1, 3, 5}. Unary: u_p = -log sigmoid((d_p - t_hi)/s), with s the std of normal-to-normal distances; pairwise: Potts with kernel w exp(-|x_p - x_q|^2/(2 theta_x^2) - (1 - cos(f_p, f_q))/theta_f), theta_x = 3 patches, theta_f = 0.1; mean-field inference, 10 iterations, on the 17x17 grid. Dependent variables: pseudo-mask Dice, false-positive components per normal-appearing region, trained pixel AUROC and Dice.
seeds.hypothesis: CRF regularisation reduces isolated false-positive components in pseudo-masks by at least 50% and increases pseudo-mask Dice by at least 6 points, and MVFA trained on CRF-regularised pseudo-masks attains higher pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities than MVFA trained on raw pseudo-masks.
seeds.method: 1) make_pseudo_masks.py: compute d_p and the label-restricted rule. 2) crf_refine.py: implement mean-field inference for a fully connected Potts CRF on 289 patches in PyTorch (dense 289x289 kernel, cheap). 3) Output q_p = P(anomalous); mask = q_p > 0.5, upsampled to 240 px; abnormal images only. 4) dataset/medical_zero.py loads the refined masks; train_zero.py unchanged. 5) w selected on source validation where source masks exist. Hyper-parameters: theta_x 3, theta_f 0.1, 10 iterations, MVFA training as in the paper.
seeds.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on the masked targets BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Checkpoints and all thresholds selected on source-modality validation splits only; MVFA re-run under the same rule as the mask-supervised reference; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; raw pseudo-masks; CRF with w in {1,3,5}; masks removed from 1 and 3 sources. Ablation: spatial-only kernel vs spatial+feature kernel. Metrics: pseudo-mask Dice, isolated FP components, trained pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC. Falsified if CRF masks do not reduce isolated components by half or if trained pixel AUROC does not improve.
provenance: G-Anomaly: A Pyramid Graph Transformer-Based Vision-Language Model for General Industrial Anomaly Detection

chain_papers: MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP
Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection

analysis.MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detect: Shows that per-image anomaly scores can be produced from dual normal/abnormal branches without a memory bank or test-set statistics. Relevant: a deployable score must depend only on references, not on other test images.
analysis.Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype: Adds a non-parametric normal-reference memory and bounds how far per-image adaptation moves the references. Relevant: a non-parametric reference distribution of normal scores is enough to make scores comparable without parametric assumptions.

seeds.rationale: MVFA's few-shot scores come from 1 - max cosine to a support memory bank and from text similarity, two scales that the code reconciles with test-set min-max. ReCAP's non-parametric normal memory suggests calibrating each branch against the empirical distribution of normal scores obtained from the supports themselves. A leave-one-out empirical CDF maps every branch and level to the same [0, 1] scale defined only by the K supports, so each test image can be scored alone and the fused score has a fixed meaning (fraction of normal patches that are less anomalous).
seeds.title: Leave-one-out empirical-CDF normalisation for inductive per-image MVFA scoring
seeds.summary: Replace test-set min-max normalisation with each branch's leave-one-out empirical CDF over support-normal patch scores, fuse in CDF space, and pool with a top-k mean.
seeds.research_idea: Independent variable: normalisation of the zero-shot and few-shot branches (test-set min-max vs. support LOO empirical CDF vs. support z-score). For level l and branch b, the reference set R_bl contains the patch scores of each support normal computed against a memory bank built from the other K-1 supports (few-shot) or against the text anchors (zero-shot). A test patch score s is mapped to F_bl(s) = (rank of s in R_bl + 0.5)/(|R_bl| + 1). The fused patch score is the mean of F over branches and levels. Image score = mean of the top 1% fused patches. Dependent variables: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity with the threshold set at the 95th percentile of support LOO image scores, realised specificity, ECE, and the per-image score shift under test-set resampling.
seeds.hypothesis: On held-out BMAD modalities with K >= 4, LOO empirical-CDF scoring keeps image AUROC within 1 point of the transductive pipeline, while each image's score is exactly invariant to test-set resampling (shift 0 vs. a median shift above 0.05 for the transductive pipeline) and the support-derived threshold gives realised specificity within 5 points of 95%.
seeds.method: 1) test_few.py: refactor into score_image(x, model, support_feats, refs) that uses no other test image. 2) utils.py: build_refs(support_feats, text_feats): for i in 1..K, memory bank from supports except i; compute few-shot patch scores of support i per level (1 - max cosine) and zero-shot scores (softmax over normal/abnormal anchors, as in MVFA); store sorted arrays R_bl. 3) cdf(s, R) via torch.searchsorted. 4) Fused map = mean over b, l of cdf maps (upsampled as in MVFA). 5) Image score = mean of top 1% pixels; threshold tau = 95th percentile of LOO image scores of the supports. 6) Remove the min-max block (test_few.py lines 220-241). Hyper-parameters: top 1%, nominal specificity 95%; no training.
seeds.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA checkpoints retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: the original transductive pipeline (test-set min-max, 0.5, max pooling) and a plain support z-score. Ordered ablation: (i) normalisation only (keep 0.5 weights and max pooling), (ii) + CDF-space fusion, (iii) + top-1% pooling. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, realised specificity, ECE (logistic map fitted on source validation), per-image score shift when 50% of the test set is resampled at 10%, 30% and 50% prevalence. Falsified if image AUROC drops by more than 1 point at K >= 4 or realised specificity misses 95% by more than 5 points.
provenance: MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP
Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection

chain_papers: Fine-Tuning CLIP Models with Convolutional Features for Medical Anomaly Detection

analysis.Fine-Tuning CLIP Models with Convolution: Keeps MVFA's multi-level adapter framework and pixel-level alignment loss while adding a ConvTokenizer; it inherits MVFA's scoring pipeline. Relevant: it shows the adapter framework transfers across implementations, so a calibration learned on source modalities for this family can plausibly transfer to an unseen modality.

seeds.rationale: Support statistics from K normal images are noisy for small K. MVFA is trained on five source modalities with validation splits, so a calibration map can be learned there: simulate few-shot episodes on each source modality's validation data, fit per-branch Platt scaling (and the fusion weight) to make scores probability-like, and transfer the fitted parameters to the held-out modality, where only the K supports are used to set the location. This separates a stable learned scale from a cheap per-modality shift.
seeds.title: Source-episode Platt calibration with support re-centring for per-image MVFA scores
seeds.summary: Learn per-branch logistic calibration and fusion weights on simulated few-shot episodes from the source modalities, then re-centre them on the target with the K support normals only.
seeds.research_idea: Independent variable: calibration (test-set min-max vs. source-episode Platt with support re-centring vs. support-only z-score). On each source modality's validation split, draw 50 episodes of K normal supports plus labelled query images; for branch b compute image-level raw scores (top-1% mean of the branch map) and fit a_b, c_b in p = sigmoid(a_b (s - mu_supp,b) + c_b) jointly over episodes, where mu_supp,b is the mean LOO support score of the episode; fit fusion weight w in logit space. On the target, only mu_supp,b is computed from its K supports. Dependent variables: image AUROC, ECE, Brier score, sensitivity at 95% specificity, per-image score shift under resampling.
seeds.hypothesis: Source-episode Platt calibration with support re-centring reduces ECE on held-out modalities by at least 50% relative to a support-only z-score while keeping image AUROC within 1 point of the transductive pipeline, and its scores are invariant to test-set resampling.
seeds.method: 1) calibrate_episodes.py: for each source modality in the training fold, load validation images; for e in 1..50, sample K normal supports and 40 queries (50% abnormal); compute branch scores with the trained model (test_few.py scoring functions); collect (s - mu_supp, label). 2) Fit a_b, c_b by logistic regression (sklearn, L2 C=1) per branch; fit w by logistic regression on the two calibrated logits. 3) Save calib.json per fold. 4) test_few.py: per-image score p = sigmoid(w1 z_zero + w2 z_few + c), z_b = a_b (s_b - mu_supp,b) + c_b, with mu_supp,b from the target supports (LOO). 5) Remove test-set min-max. Hyper-parameters: 50 episodes, 40 queries, K matched to the target K.
seeds.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA checkpoints retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: the original transductive pipeline (test-set min-max, 0.5, max pooling) and a plain support z-score. Ordered ablation: (i) support re-centring only, (ii) + source-episode Platt scale, (iii) + learned fusion weight. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, ECE (15 bins), Brier, sensitivity at 95% specificity, per-image shift under resampling (10-50% prevalence). Falsified if ECE is not reduced by 50% versus the support-only z-score or if image AUROC drops by more than 1 point.
provenance: Fine-Tuning CLIP Models with Convolutional Features for Medical Anomaly Detection

chain_papers: Fed-LoRA: Cross-Domain Generative Knowledge Feedback for Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection

analysis.Fed-LoRA: Cross-Domain Generative Knowle: Synthesises abnormal exemplars matched to a site's imaging style, showing that synthetic abnormal images are a useful stand-in when real abnormal data are scarce. Relevant: synthetic anomalies in the target's own support images can provide an 'abnormal' reference point without any real abnormal target data.

seeds.rationale: Min-max normalisation needs two anchors, a low and a high value; MVFA takes both from the test set. The K support normals provide the low anchor, but nothing in the target provides a high anchor. Following Fed-LoRA's use of style-matched synthetic abnormal exemplars, synthetic lesions pasted into the target's own support normals can provide the high anchor: scale each branch so that support normals map to 0 and synthetic lesions map to 1. This keeps MVFA's two-anchor logic while removing the dependence on the test set.
seeds.title: Two-anchor scaling with support normals and synthetic lesions for inductive MVFA scoring
seeds.summary: Normalise each MVFA branch between the median score of the support normals and the median score of synthetic lesions pasted into those supports, so no test-set statistics are needed.
seeds.research_idea: Independent variable: normalisation (test-set min-max vs. two-anchor synthetic scaling vs. support z-score). For each branch b and level l: lo_bl = median LOO patch score over support-normal patches; hi_bl = median patch score over pasted-lesion pixels in 20 synthetic variants per support (CutPaste-style patches from other supports plus Gaussian intensity blobs, 1-5% of the image area). Normalised score z = (s - lo)/(hi - lo), clipped to [-1, 3]; fused with weight 0.5 (then learned on source episodes in the ablation); image score = top-1% mean. Dependent variables: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity with tau from support LOO scores, per-image score shift under resampling.
seeds.hypothesis: Two-anchor synthetic scaling keeps image AUROC within 1 point of the transductive pipeline at K >= 4 and yields lower ECE than a support-only z-score, because the synthetic anchor fixes the scale between branches.
seeds.method: 1) synth.py: synth_lesion(img) with CutPaste from another support image and Gaussian-intensity blobs; masks recorded. 2) utils.py: anchors(model, supports): LOO normal patch scores and synthetic-lesion patch scores per branch and level; lo, hi = medians. 3) test_few.py: score_image applies (s - lo)/(hi - lo), clip [-1, 3], fuse 0.5/0.5, top-1% pooling; remove test-set min-max. 4) Threshold tau = 95th percentile of support LOO image scores. Hyper-parameters: 20 synthetic variants per support, area 1-5%, clip range [-1, 3]; no training.
seeds.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA checkpoints retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: the original transductive pipeline (test-set min-max, 0.5, max pooling) and a plain support z-score. Ordered ablation: (i) two-anchor normalisation, (ii) + learned fusion weight on source episodes, (iii) + top-1% pooling. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, ECE, sensitivity at 95% specificity, realised specificity, score shift under resampling. Falsified if AUROC drops by more than 1 point or ECE is not lower than with the support z-score.
provenance: Fed-LoRA: Cross-Domain Generative Knowledge Feedback for Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection

chain_papers: Bridging Vision Foundation Model Priors with CLIP for Spatial-aware Few-shot Anomaly Detection in Medical Images

analysis.Bridging Vision Foundation Model Priors: Stores compact normal and abnormal prototypes of the support set and fuses patch-to-prototype with image-text similarities, reducing memory while improving localisation. Relevant: prototypes have natural radii (within-cluster spread), which give a scale for distances that does not depend on the test set.

seeds.rationale: The few-shot branch's raw score (1 - max cosine to the bank) has no intrinsic scale: what counts as far depends on how spread the normal patches are at that level and location. Spatial-FAD's prototypes suggest a scale: express each test patch's distance to its nearest normal prototype in units of that prototype's radius. This makes the few-shot branch scale-free per level, and the zero-shot branch can be scaled in the same way with support LOO statistics, so both branches are comparable without test-set min-max.
seeds.title: Prototype-radius normalisation of MVFA's few-shot branch for per-image scoring
seeds.summary: Cluster the support patch features into normal prototypes per level, score test patches by distance to the nearest prototype divided by its radius, and fuse with a support-standardised zero-shot branch.
seeds.research_idea: Independent variable: few-shot branch scoring (MVFA bank + test-set min-max vs. prototype-radius score vs. bank score with support z-score). Per level l: k-means (k = min(32, K*17*17/20)) on support patch features; radius r_k = 90th percentile of member distances. Test patch score q = min_k ||f - P_k|| / r_k. Zero-shot branch: support LOO z-score. Fusion: mean of the two after a log1p transform of q; image score top-1% mean. Dependent variables: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, per-image score shift, memory and latency.
seeds.hypothesis: Prototype-radius scoring matches the memory-bank few-shot branch within 1 point of pixel AUROC at K >= 4 and makes the fused per-image score invariant to test-set composition, while reducing the few-shot memory by at least 10x.
seeds.method: 1) utils.py: fit_prototypes(support_feats_l, k) with torch k-means (20 iterations); radii as 90th percentiles. 2) test_few.py: few-shot map = min_k ||f - P_k||/r_k per level; log1p; zero-shot map standardised by support LOO mean/std; fused mean over levels and branches; remove test-set min-max. 3) Image score top-1% mean; tau from support LOO image scores. 4) Report memory (number of stored vectors) and latency per image. Hyper-parameters: k as above, 90th percentile radius, 20 k-means iterations; no training.
seeds.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA checkpoints retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: the original transductive pipeline (test-set min-max, 0.5, max pooling) and a plain support z-score. Ordered ablation: (i) prototype scoring with the original min-max (isolates the scoring), (ii) inductive normalisation, (iii) top-1% pooling. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, score shift under resampling, memory, latency. Falsified if pixel AUROC drops by more than 1 point at K >= 4.
provenance: Bridging Vision Foundation Model Priors with CLIP for Spatial-aware Few-shot Anomaly Detection in Medical Images

chain_papers: AA-CLIP: Enhancing Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection via Anomaly-Aware CLIP
PSMP-CLIP: Patch-Prompt SAM and Multi-Semantic Prompting for CLIP-Based Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection

analysis.AA-CLIP: Enhancing Zero-Shot Anomaly Det: Creates anomaly-aware text anchors so that the normal/abnormal similarity is well separated, then aligns patch features with them. Relevant: when anchors are well separated, the zero-shot branch's softmax over the two anchors is already a probability-like score that needs only a temperature, not test-set min-max.
analysis.PSMP-CLIP: Patch-Prompt SAM and Multi-Se: Samples prompts from patch features to avoid threshold drift when converting CLIP maps into masks. Relevant: it identifies threshold drift, the dependence of a binarisation threshold on the score distribution at hand, as a core weakness of CLIP-based maps.

seeds.rationale: MVFA's zero-shot branch is a two-way softmax over normal/abnormal text anchors, so it is already on a probability scale, and min-max normalising it over the test set destroys that meaning and causes threshold drift. A temperature fitted on source validation restores calibration; the few-shot branch can be mapped to a probability with a logistic fitted to support LOO scores and source episodes. Fusing the two in log-odds space (product of experts) gives a principled per-image probability and a threshold that does not drift.
seeds.title: Log-odds fusion of temperature-calibrated MVFA branches for inductive scoring
seeds.summary: Calibrate the zero-shot branch with a source-fitted temperature, map the few-shot branch to a probability with support statistics, and add the two log-odds instead of min-max normalising and averaging.
seeds.research_idea: Independent variable: fusion rule (test-set min-max + 0.5 average vs. log-odds sum of calibrated branches vs. average of calibrated probabilities). Zero-shot: p0 = softmax(T^-1 [s_abn, s_norm]) with T fitted on source validation pixels (masked sources) and images (all sources). Few-shot: p1 = sigmoid((d - mu_supp)/sigma_supp * a + c) with a, c fitted on source episodes and mu, sigma from target support LOO. Fused logit = logit(p0) + logit(p1) - logit(pi), pi the source prevalence prior; image score = top-1% mean of fused probabilities. Dependent variables: image/pixel AUROC, ECE, sensitivity at 95% specificity with the fixed threshold 0.5 and with support-derived thresholds, threshold drift across held-out modalities.
seeds.hypothesis: Log-odds fusion of calibrated branches keeps image AUROC within 1 point of the transductive pipeline and halves ECE, and the fixed threshold 0.5 yields realised specificity that varies by at most 10 points across held-out modalities (versus more than 25 points for a threshold on min-max scores).
seeds.method: 1) calibrate.py: fit T by minimising NLL of the zero-shot pixel/image predictions on source validation (LBFGS); fit a, c by logistic regression on source episodes (as in Platt scaling). 2) test_few.py: compute p0, p1 per pixel; fused = sigmoid(logit p0 + logit p1 - logit pi); remove test-set min-max; image score = top-1% mean. 3) Report specificity at fixed threshold 0.5 and at support-derived tau. Hyper-parameters: T init 1, LBFGS 100 iterations, 50 episodes; no adapter training.
seeds.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA checkpoints retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: the original transductive pipeline (test-set min-max, 0.5, max pooling) and a plain support z-score. Ordered ablation: (i) calibrated branches with average fusion, (ii) log-odds fusion, (iii) top-1% pooling. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, ECE, Brier, sensitivity/specificity at 0.5 and at tau, spread of realised specificity across held-out modalities. Falsified if AUROC drops more than 1 point or ECE is not halved.
provenance: AA-CLIP: Enhancing Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection via Anomaly-Aware CLIP
PSMP-CLIP: Patch-Prompt SAM and Multi-Semantic Prompting for CLIP-Based Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection

chain_papers: G-Anomaly: A Pyramid Graph Transformer-Based Vision-Language Model for General Industrial Anomaly Detection

analysis.G-Anomaly: A Pyramid Graph Transformer-B: Preserves the structural relations between image regions with a graph encoder so that anomalous regions are distinguished from texture. It is industrial, not medical, and builds on MVFA only indirectly; its insight that anomalies are coherent regions rather than single patches is used here for aggregation.

seeds.rationale: MVFA's image score is the maximum fused pixel, which one spurious pixel can decide. G-Anomaly's view that anomalies are coherent regions suggests aggregating at region level: threshold the fused map at a support-derived level, form connected regions, and score an image by its strongest region's mass (mean excess score times area). Combined with support-standardised branches, this gives a per-image score that is robust to isolated spikes and needs no test-set statistics.
seeds.title: Region-mass aggregation with support-derived thresholds for robust per-image MVFA scores
seeds.summary: Standardise both branches with support LOO statistics, threshold the fused map at a support-derived level, and score each image by the excess mass of its strongest connected region.
seeds.research_idea: Independent variable: image aggregation (max pixel vs. top-1% mean vs. region mass), with support z-score normalisation in all inductive variants. Region mass: tau_pix = 99th percentile of support LOO fused pixel scores; regions = 8-connected components of {x: m(x) > tau_pix}; mass(R) = sum_{x in R} (m(x) - tau_pix); image score = max_R mass(R) (0 if no region). Dependent variables: image AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, AUROC drop under injection of 1-5 spurious single-patch spikes into normal test maps, per-image score shift under resampling.
seeds.hypothesis: Region-mass aggregation keeps image AUROC within 1 point of max pooling on clean data and loses at most one third as much AUROC as max pooling when 3 spurious spikes are injected into normal test maps.
seeds.method: 1) test_few.py: support LOO z-scores per branch and level; fused map m = mean; remove test-set min-max. 2) utils.py: region_mass(m, tau) with scipy.ndimage.label (8-connectivity). 3) tau_pix from support LOO fused maps (99th percentile); image threshold tau_img = 95th percentile of support LOO image scores. 4) Stress test: inject k in {1, 3, 5} single-patch spikes (value = 99.9th percentile of the image's map + 3 std) at random positions in normal test maps. Hyper-parameters: percentiles 99 and 95; no training.
seeds.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA checkpoints retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: the original transductive pipeline (test-set min-max, 0.5, max pooling) and a plain support z-score. Ordered ablation: (i) support z-score normalisation with max pooling, (ii) top-1% mean, (iii) region mass. Metrics: image AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, AUROC under spike injection, score shift under resampling. Falsified if region mass loses more than 1 point of clean AUROC or does not reduce the injected-spike AUROC drop by at least half.
provenance: G-Anomaly: A Pyramid Graph Transformer-Based Vision-Language Model for General Industrial Anomaly Detection
